title: test(metadata-protocol): lock-one-resolution takes each distinct read request's reads once, 20 s to 8.4 s (#23182 row 1)
body:
Part of #23182 (row 1)
Clause-②: no

This PR covers row 1 of #23182 only: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `src/protocol.lock-one-resolution.test.ts`, 113.2 s in run `38228297391`. It changes one test file and no production file. It takes the file from about 20 s to about 8.4 s alone on this box, and it does **not** by itself get the file under the 10 s line under CI-shaped contention (27.5 s in the package-suite reading below). The fork that is left is a maintainer's call; it is under "What is left" and in the dev report. #23182 stays open: this PR does not close row 1, and row 5 is its own card of work.

## Where the time went

Measured at BASE `534ca13eb5` (vitest module line, default reporter, a shared 4-core box under `os-verify-lock`):

- The file is 16 320 generated rows plus 40 named tests. Each row runs under both orders the store can return its stored rows in and both orders its packages can be registered in, so the rows make **28 848 runs** of (a fresh protocol instance, two reads, one door).
- Per category, summed over the run, from an instrumented copy: `getMetaItem` 6.9 s and `getMetaItemLayered` 4.9 s (28 875 calls each), the doors 2.25 s, `vi.spyOn` 0.77 s, building the instances 0.48 s, and about 5.5 s for matchers, the oracle and the runner.
- None of it is waiting. There is no timer, lease or sleep in the file, and the per-call times (0.1 to 0.4 ms) add up to the module line: it is CPU.
- The reads take no organization and no verb (`envelope` ignores its organization argument, and neither read has a verb). The table's rows that differ only in `requestScope` and `operation` therefore asked the same two reads of the same data four times each: **28 848 read runs against 7 212 distinct requests**, exactly 4 to 1.

## What changed (test only)

- **`readScenario`:** one protocol instance per distinct read request, its two reads taken once. The key is the request's real inputs: the environment, the stored rows and the artifacts in the order the store and the registry return them, the type spelling and the package. It is not a description of a row, so two rows share an instance only when every input the reads take is byte-equal. The instance a row's door then runs on is the one its reads ran on, so the header's "ONE protocol instance" still holds (a read still precedes every door on its instance). What is new is that a door can also follow another door on that instance; every row passes under both shapes, and the red sets below are equal on both.
- **The oracle is asked once per row,** not once per order (`expectedLock` was called five times per run).
- **`agree`:** `expect(actual, message).toEqual(expected)` for the table's hot path. `isDeepStrictEqual` implies `toEqual`'s equality, so when a pair is strictly equal the matcher would pass and is not built; when a pair differs the real matcher runs and fails with the message and diff it always gave. The table made well over a hundred thousand matchers (about 2 s of the wall).
- **Not changed:** every `expect` that the rows made is still made on the same pair, the 16 360 tests keep their titles and their order, no case is deleted, skipped or moved, and no timeout is touched. `door` still ends at the real `saveMetaItem` / `deleteMetaItem`: a refusal anywhere in the write path is still the verdict (I did not stop the write at the gate, because "end to end" is what the door's doc says it pins).

## Wall time

Vitest module line in ms, a shared 4-core box under `os-verify-lock`, `--maxWorkers=2`, file alone; BASE and AFTER runs interleaved:

| | BASE `534ca13eb5` | AFTER `f214779c15` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| file alone, 3 runs | 19542 / 20389 / 19742 (a first run read 21401) | 8404 / 9133 / 8419 (the earlier head `6717655b7f`, same code: 8258 / 8359 / 8779) |
| whole package, `--maxWorkers=8` (2x oversubscribed) | 58433 | 27511 |
| heap used at the end of the file | 954 MB | 774 MB |

- **Whole package:** 236 files passed and 3 skipped, 20 566 tests passed and 19 skipped, before and after.
- **CI after this change:** NOT MEASURED here (job logs redirect to a blob host the egress proxy refuses). The 27.5 s package-suite reading is the nearest stand-in for CI's contention, and it is over the line.
- **What the 8.4 s is made of now.** An instrumented copy of the memo-only head (`1dc5a6150e`, 10.8 s) read: the two reads 3.7 s (7 239 calls of each), the doors 2.0 s, `vi.spyOn` 0.55 s, the rest of the row bodies 3.2 s and the runner 1.4 s. The hoist and `agree` then took about 2 s out of the last two. So the protocol's own calls, the reads and the doors, are about 5.7 s of the 8.4 s, and they cannot be shared further without changing what a row asks.

## Ablation: the pins still go red, on the same rows

Each leg mutated production source through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 to 0, the replacement counted, the blob changed), ran a temporary copy of the BASE file and this branch's file in one vitest run, and was restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty. The subject is imported by relative path from `src`, so no `dist` is in play. The temporary BASE copy is deleted.

| leg | mutation | red tests, BASE file | red tests, this branch | failing titles |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|:--|
| A1 | the item lock joins only the first shipping package's answer (`item-lock.ts`) | 2384 | 2384 | equal sets |
| A2 | the write doors ignore the stored rows (`item-lock.ts`, `resolveItemLockLazily`) | 1823 | 1823 | equal sets |
| A3 | the served body no longer carries the resolved lock family (`item-lock.ts`, `withItemLockFamily`) | 7744 | 7744 | equal sets |
| A4 | an organization-scoped write is no longer refused first (`protocol.ts`, temporary, restored) | 8160 | 8160 | equal sets |

The first failure of A2 reads "the door: expected 'admitted' to deeply equal ..." on both files, so the failing path of `agree` reports the message and diff the plain matcher did.

## Verification at `f214779c15`

- **Typecheck:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol typecheck` exits 0; `tsc --listFiles` names the test file once.
- **Lint (narrowed to the one file):** `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` reports 1 file, 0 errors and 0 warnings. `--print-config` returns a config for the file, and its parserOptions are `ecmaVersion` and `sourceType` only, so type-aware linting is off and this diff cannot move any other file's result.
- **Gates:** `dispatch-gates` over the one path derives 51 commands. All 114 distinct commands (the 51, plus the 53 artifact-roster and 11 wide-population families it names, one shared) ran at this head after a full `turbo run build` (74 tasks): 110 exit 0 and 4 exit non-zero. The 4 are PR-context guards that judged nothing and say so: `check-closing-target-claim` (2) and `check-single-claim-paths` (2) need a PR number and a token, `check-governed-queue-guard` (1) needs the event payload, `check-partof-closing-keyword` (2) needs a PR body (re-run below with this body). They are NOT MEASURED, not red.
- **Bytes:** `check:nul-bytes` exits 0 (inside the 114).

## No changeset

This diff changes only a test file under `packages/metadata-protocol/src`, which `files` (`dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`) does not ship. `skip-changeset` is the label, as on the earlier rows.

## What is left (the fork)

The single file's floor on this box is about 8.4 s, of which 5.7 s is the protocol's own calls over the 7 212 distinct reads and 28 848 doors. Under CI's contention that is about 27 s. Two routes get the file off the next refresh's list, and neither is mine to take:

- **B. Split the rows over K files** that each keep the memo, partitioned so that the four rows sharing a read stay together. A prototype partition (scratch, deleted) measured, alone: K=2 at 5.4 / 4.8 s and K=4 at 2.8 / 2.8 / 3.3 / 2.8 s, each including the 40 named tests. It needs a shared test-only helper, a pin that every shard file exists (a deleted shard would silently drop rows), and, if the engine double moves into the helper, a change to its entry in `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`. It costs one import of `protocol.ts` per extra file.
- **C. A named exception** for the file, as #23247 ruled for row 3 (#23296). None of the two `test-budget` classes in `measure-test-shard-timings.mjs` names a generated-product enumeration, so it needs a ruling for the class as well as for the file. Only the maintainer grants it.

## Acceptance notes

- This row's pin is the next refresh PR's list no longer naming the file. This PR alone is not expected to meet it.
- Outside the module line: a single-file run spends about 13 s in vitest's import phase here (transform 10 s, cold). Observation only; carrier: none.
